statement: In H=L²((0,infinity),dx), let rho_a(x)={1/(a x)}, chi=1_(0,1], and B_nat=span{rho_a:a in positive integers}. RH iff chi belongs to the H closure of B_nat (Theorem1.1, pp.1–2).

For B_lambda=span{{theta/t}:lambda<=theta<=1} in L²((0,infinity),dt), D(lambda)=dist(chi,B_lambda), liminf_{lambda↓0}D(lambda)*sqrt(log(1/lambda)) >= sqrt(sum_rho m_rho²/|rho|²) (Theorem1.3 p.4; Theorem5.5 pp.15–16). Proof assumes RH, since its failure makes the left side infinite; rho are distinct nontrivial zeros under that assumption.
Theorem1.4: Q of positive degree with all roots alpha on the unit circle, multiplicities m_alpha, and fixed target polynomial P gives lim N inf_deg A<=N ||P-QA||²=sum_alpha m_alpha²|P(alpha)|².

Assume RH and sum_{|Im rho|<=T}|zeta'(rho)|^(-2)<<T^(3/2-delta) for some delta>0. For V_N(s)=sum_{n<=N}(1-log n/log N)mu(n)n^(-s), N>1, its squared weighted critical-line error (1/(2pi))integral_R |1-zeta(1/2+it)V_N(1/2+it)|² dt/(1/4+t²) is asymptotic to (2+gamma-log(4pi))/log N (Theorem1,p.2). Moment hypothesis forces simple zeros.
For Q=(1-z)^2, BCF linear reciprocal window has exact squared H² error 1+4/N, N>=1.
For Q=(1-z)^2 and degree bound N>=0, optimal coefficients are (n+1)(L-n)(L-n-1)/((L+1)(L+2)), L=N+2; squared distance is 2(2L+1)/((L+1)(L+2)).
For Q_theta=(1-z)(1-exp(-i theta)z), degree bound N, L=N+2,d=L+1,S=sum exp(i k theta), k=0..L, theta not multiple2pi, squared optimal H² error=(2d-2ReS)/(d²-|S|²).
For fixed c!=0, L E_N(c/L) tends to (2-2sin(c)/c)/(1-(2sin(c/2)/c)^2), extending to4 at c=0 and tending to2 as |c|→infinity.

For the two-root polynomial Q_theta, triangular reciprocal window squared error equals [2N+2ReT+|T|²]/N², T=sum_{k=1}^N exp(-ik theta). If theta=c/N, it tends (2sin(c/2)/c)², whereas the optimum tends0.

For every C>=0,N>=0,L=N+2, |c|<=C, the actual optimum E_N for Q_theta=(1-z)(1-exp(-i theta)z) satisfies |L E_N(c/L)-F(c)|<=38(12+C²)²/L, where F(c)=(2-2sin(c)/c)/(1-(2sin(c/2)/c)²), F(0)=4; aliases use the true double-root optimum. If L>=6(12+C²), the bound improves to [2(12+C²)²+5(12+C²)]/L.
